# Refined source control study

Six unchanged complete sources and twelve actual CLI observations join the
existing source ctrl sector gate with original finite Meaning requests. This
is informed repository work, not a blind model benchmark; no external model
was invoked. Sources and baseline refusals were saved before implementation.

The baseline refuses all six: four at the unsupported control boundary and two
at the latent Meaning boundary after audit-root expansion. The repaired path
accepts Z followed by independently specified X, an identity entry whose unused
control-bearing body contains a valid X request, and an independently specified
Z provider that itself uses ctrl. It rejects Hadamard on a ctrl owner, a false
identity request on X, and that same false request inside an unused audit body.
These now fail actual contract checks, rather than an unsupported-path guard.

Independent Rust tests check literal exact matrices for all three positives.
Private-boundary tests confirm that audit expansion adds checked Meaning leaves
while retaining the original selected root. A shared-budget regression gives
only enough work for the finite equation and requires the subsequent native
sector replay to reject; a hidden fresh default budget would incorrectly pass.
Missing checkers and zero work reject. The first missing-checker test expected
`lean_checker`, but the existing transport reports `io`; only that test
expectation was corrected. No source or original observation was rewritten.

Every original control obligation still needs retained concrete coverage, and
all concrete specializations and unused bodies remain checked. Unclosed generics,
erased intervals and symbolic inverse/control of a ctrl-bearing body remain
unsupported. These checks do not prove AST preservation or full QS/PR/RS, add a
constitutional guarantee, complete #83/#46, change native acceptance/protocol,
or permit a fallback. Rectangular Meaning evidence remains open.
